authority.epoch_convention: notes/plan/schemas/README.md (Identity; What advances a schema epoch)

base_resolution.default: git merge-base HEAD main, falling back to origin/main
base_resolution.degradation: No resolvable base means SKIP: the reason is printed on stderr, the report carries "status": "skip" and the resolution trail, and the delta rules are reported as not enforced. Exit 0 by default so a fresh clone does not fail the local gate; exit 1 under --require-base, which is how CI states that a base is owed. There is no path on which an unenforced run reports a pass.
base_resolution.explicit: --base <rev>; an explicit base that does not resolve is a hard failure
base_resolution.head_default: the working tree (untracked files included); --head <rev> for a revision

boundary: Two revisions, not a history: this compares a base to a head and does not look at the commits in between, so an edit made and reverted inside a branch is correctly invisible and a squashed force-push is judged on its result. `Semantic change` is approximated by `the comment-stripped code of a semantic-tier file changed`, which over-approximates (a local rename counts) and under-approximates in one narrow corner (a change confined to run-of-spaces inside a string literal). Whether the cited decision record actually governs the change, and whether a published compatibility verdict is the correct one, are review judgements no diff can make: this proves the record and the statement exist and shipped with the change. The epoch rule reads schema documents only — an IDL or RFC edit that breaks a contract without touching a schema file is out of its scope.
determinism: This file records no timestamp, commit id, or absolute path: it is a function of the repository contents alone, so an unchanged tree reproduces it byte-for-byte. The real run's verdict is deliberately not recorded here — it is a function of two revisions, not of the tree — and is reported to stdout and to CI instead.

freeze_regime.fail_closed: An absent or reworded schemas/README.md is read as `in force`.
freeze_regime.in_force: Clause absent (or --freeze in-force): the same findings are violations.
freeze_regime.pre_freeze: While the clause is present, epoch 1 is a draft edited in place: `schema-bytes-changed-without-epoch-advance` and `published-schema-document-deleted` findings are DEFERRED — printed and reported, not failures.

GOV-1-08.enforces: A semantic-tier source file whose code changed between the base and the head must cite a numbered decision record at head, unless the delta itself adds or modifies one; a source file the delta *adds* must cite one regardless. `Semantic tier` is check_code_policy.SEMANTIC_CORE, imported rather than re-declared. Comment-only and formatting-only edits are not semantic changes.

GOV-1-09.enforces: A schema document whose bytes changed with `schema_epoch` unchanged, or which was deleted, is a violation once the PR 5 freeze is in force; a `schema_epoch` that retreats, and an advance published without its typed `Preserved | Revalidate | Incompatible` statement in the same delta, are violations in every regime.

base_resolution_cases.reason: not inside a git work tree, or `git` is unavailable: `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` exited 127
not inside a git work tree, or `git` is unavailable: `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` exited 128
HEAD does not name a commit (unborn branch or empty repository); there is no head revision to diff against
no trunk base is resolvable: main: unknown ref; origin/main: unknown ref
no trunk base is resolvable: main: no common ancestor with HEAD (shallow checkout or unrelated history); origin/main: no common ancestor with HEAD (shallow checkout or unrelated history)
--base 'no-such-rev' does not resolve to a commit; an explicit base that is wrong is a failure, not a reason to skip
`git diff --name-only 0123456789ab` exited 128; the delta could not be computed
`git ls-files --others` exited 128; untracked files could not be listed, so an added-but-unstaged source would be invisible to the delta rules
